final.title: Privacy promises do not control your workflow
final.body:
If you are bringing AI into a small business, privacy promises are only part of the picture. A vendor can tell you where data is stored, how it is protected, and what terms apply. That still does not answer the operational question that matters most: who is allowed to act on the data once it is in your workflow.

That is the first decision I would make. For any repeatable process, such as invoice handling or customer replies, decide whether the AI may act on its own or only recommend an action and wait for human approval. For money movement and other high-risk decisions, human approval stays mandatory. That is policy, not optimism.

The reason is simple: privacy terms do not run your approvals. If your workflow is loose, a careful vendor will not fix that. If your workflow is tight, you can use AI without handing over the keys to the shop.

A useful question to ask any tool is: will I see the input, the reasoning, and the recommended action before anything is committed?

Then map your most repeated workflow, mark the points where money, customer communication, or data deletion could happen, and decide which of those points must stay human-approved.
